en: The Names of the Twenty-eight Great Yakṣa Army Kings, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghabara.
Excerpted from the Buddha’s address to Ānanda: “You should receive and uphold the names of the twenty-eight great yakṣa army kings to protect [the ten directions].”
Ānanda, in the eastern direction there are four yakṣa generals who dwell in the eastern region and constantly protect the east;
their names are as follows:
Dīrghanakha (in the Liang language, "Long"), Sunetra (in the Liang language, "Good Eye"), Pūrṇaka (in the Liang language, "Full"), and Kapila (in the Liang language, "Blue-Black").
Ānanda, furthermore, there are four yakṣas residing in the south who constantly protect the southern direction;
their names are as follows:
Saṃgha (in the Liang language, "Lion"), Upasaṃgha (in the Liang language, "Son of the Lion"), Śaṅkara (in the Liang language, "Conch"), and Caṇḍana (in the Liang language...).
Candana. Ānanda, furthermore, there are four yakṣas dwelling in the western direction who reside in the west to protect it; their names are as follows.
Hārīti (in the Liang language, "Lion"), Hārītikīśa (in the Liang language, "Lion’s Hair"), Varuṇa (in the Liang language, "Sovereign"), and Pingala (in the Liang language, "Azure").
Furthermore, there are four yakṣas in the north who dwell in the north and constantly protect the northern quarter; these are their names.
Thus it is: Dhāraṇa (Liang: "Holding"), Dhārananda (Liang: "Joy"), Ugraparākrama (Liang: "Vigorous Guarding"), and Vetravana (Liang: "Enclosure").
Ānanda, in the four intermediate directions there are four yakṣas who dwell in those four intermediate directions, constantly guarding them; their names are as follows:
Pañcika (in the Liang language, "Five"), Pañcāla-candra (in the Liang language, "Five Terrifying Ones"), and Saptaparṇi (in the Liang language, "Seven Mountains").
[The Lord] Khaṇḍa-campata (in the Liang language, "Lord of the Snow Mountains") said:
"Ānanda, in the lower direction there are four yakṣa generals who dwell in the lower direction and constantly protect it;
their names are as follows."
Bhūma (in the Liang language, "Earth"), Subhūma (in the Liang language, "Good Earth"), Kāla (in the Liang language, "Black"), and Upakāla (in the Liang language, "Little Black")— above,
there are four yakṣa generals who dwell above and constantly protect the upper regions;
their names are as follows.
Soma (in the Liang language, "Moon"), Śūri (in the Liang language, "Sun"), Aukhani (in the Liang language, "Fire"), and Vāyu (in the Liang language, "Wind")—
after the Buddha had explained to Ānanda these characteristics of the great majesty and power that benefit the twenty-eight divisions of the yakṣa generals,
this teaching is called the "Dharma for the Protection of the State."
